1.w: [“] Can you draw out Leviathan with a hook, and press down his tongue with a rope?

2.w: Can you put a cord in his nose, and with a hook pierce his jaw?

3.w: Will he multiply to you supplications? Indeed, will he speak to you softly?

4.w: Will he cut a covenant with you, to take him as a slave forever?

5.w: Will you play with him like a bird, and leash him for your maidens?

6.w: Will traders barter for him? Will they divide him among the merchants?

7.w: Can you fill his skin with harpoons, or his head with spears of fishing?

8.w: Put your hands on him; may you remember the battle, [and] not add.

9.w: Behold, the hope of him is false. [One is] even cast down at the sight of him.

10.w: None [is] so fierce that he would rouse him; and who is he who will stand before my face?

11.w: Who has brought before Me that I should repay [him]? Under all the heavens it [is] unto Me.

12.w: I will not keep silent about his limbs, and the matter of his strength and the grace of his form.

13.w: Who can uncover the face of his clothing? Who can enter into the double of his bridle?

14.w: The doors of his face, who can open [them]? All around his teeth [are] terror.

15.w: [His] rows of shields are [his] pride, shut up tight with a seal.

16.w: One by one they draw near, and air cannot come between them.

17.w: They are joined a man to his brother; they clasp together and cannot be separated.

18.w: His sneezings flash forth light, and his eyes [are] like the eyelids of the dawn.

19.w: From his mouth torches go forth; sparks of fire leap out.

20.w: From his nostrils smoke comes forth, boiling like a pot and a reed.

21.w: His breath will kindle the coals, and a flame goes forth from his mouth.

22.w: In his neck lodges strength, and before him terror dances.

23.w: The folds of his flesh are joined together, c on him, [and] it annot be shaken.

24.w: His heart is as firm as a stone, even as firm as a lower millstone.

25.w: From his rising up the mighty are afraid; before his thrashing they cleanse themselves from sin.

26.w: The sword reaching him shall not stand—[not] spear, dart, or lance.

27.w: He regards iron as straw, [and] bronze as rotten wood.

28.w: The son of the bow cannot make him flee; the stones of the sling are turned over before him like stubble.

29.w: A club is regarded as stubble, and he laughs at the rattle of a lance.

30.w: Beneath him are points of a shard; he spreads out like a threshing sledge upon the mud.

31.w: He makes the deep boil like a pot; he makes the sea like an ointment pot.

32.w: Behind him he makes a path shine; one would think the deep [were] white-haired.

33.w: There is nothing on earth like him, the one made devoid of fear.

34.w: He beholds every high [thing]; he [is] king over all the sons of pride.”
